Fuji Recipes is a dedicated offline companion for Fujifilm X-series photographers. It allows you to collect, create, organize, and fine-tune film simulation recipes directly from your phone.
With direct USB camera connection support, you can seamlessly read and write custom recipe presets to your camera\'s custom slots without relying on internet connectivity or cloud servers.
Your recipes are stored on this phone and nowhere else. Export to back them up or move them to another device, and import to read one back.
This application has been developed and tested on Google Pixel devices with a Fujifilm X-T50 camera body.

This phone has no USB host support
Writing to a camera needs USB host mode, which this device does not have. Storing and editing recipes works normally.
Connect the camera with a USB-C cable and set its USB mode to the RAW-conversion/backup mode.

The slot is being changed right now. Stopping leaves it partly written, which is neither the old recipe nor the new one.
Read the recipes saved in your camera\'s C1–C7 slots
Import reads the custom recipe slots saved on the camera itself. Connect it with a USB-C cable, set its USB mode to the RAW-conversion/backup mode, and this screen will be ready.
Reading looks at all seven custom slots and does not change anything on the camera.
The camera\'s custom slots are empty, so there is nothing to import. Recipes appear here once they are saved to C1–C7 on the body.
Everything on the camera is already in your library. The slots are listed below if you want a second copy of one anyway.

Save your recipes to a file and share it anywhere
Builds the file on this phone. The share sheet takes it from there — Files, Drive, a message, anything installed. This is how a library gets backed up or moved to another device.
Export saves your recipes to a file you can keep or move to another phone. Make your first one and it will be waiting here.
Every selected recipe in a single file. The easiest to keep and to read back in.
One file per recipe inside an archive. Better when you want to pick individual recipes out later.
The export could not be prepared, so nothing left the app: %1$s
Choose a JPEG from your Fujifilm camera and this extracts the recipe it was shot with, then tells you whether it is one you already have. It all happens on this phone.
Every setting the photo carries matches that recipe.
Nothing in your library matches closely enough to name. You can save this as a new recipe.
Your library is empty, so there is nothing to compare against yet.
This reads the recipe out of a JPEG your camera wrote. A RAF file is not one — if you shoot RAW+JPEG, choose the JPEG.
Photos up to 50 MB can be read. A camera JPEG is far smaller than that, so this is usually a RAW file.
Its EXIF has been stripped, which usually means it was edited, exported or sent through an app that removes it. The original from the camera will still have it.
This photo has metadata, but not the Fujifilm recipe block. Only JPEGs written by a Fujifilm camera carry it.

It looks like a Fujifilm JPEG, but its recipe block is not in a form this app can walk. If the file was re-saved by another app, try the camera original.
